body:
Current requirements that require re-authentication as a defense.

| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **7.5.1** | Verify that the application requires re-authentication before allowing modifications to sensitive account attributes which may affect authentication such as email address, phone number, MFA configuration, or other information used in account recovery. | 2 | v5.0.be-3.7.1 |
| **7.5.2** | Verify that users are able to view and (having re-entered login credentials) terminate any or all currently active sessions. | 2 | v5.0.be-3.7.2 |
| **7.5.3** | Verify that the application requires re-authentication or secondary verification before performing highly sensitive transactions or operations. | 3 | v5.0.be-3.7.3 |


| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **13.2.3** | Verify that, if the application allows changing configurations around passwords or connection parameters for integrations with external databases and services, they are protected by extra controls such as re-authentication or multi-user approval. | 2 | v5.0.be-14.7.3 |

I think those are a bit username-password authentication era oriented. In ASVS v5.0 MFA is required from L2 (as msot of the listed requirements) and it is easy to interpet, that full MFA authentication is required to satisfy those requirements.

But is this the case? Or for example, single-factor or an alternative TOTP-based authentication is ok here?

comments.body:
I often see services like wise (payment service) just ask for a password again, I rarely see re-auth for user account data forcing MFA.

But for some L3 apps I see more MFA before I can transfer money or move coins around.

Hmmm. 

Maybe for 7.5.1 + 7.5.1 (L2) we just allow single factor re-auth but for 7.5.3 (l3) require MFA re-auth.

I'm not sure about 13.2.3.

So I would rather leave 7.5.3 vague as it is already a slightly vague requirement. Same for 13.2.3. Both of these are going to be very open to interpretation whatever happens so I don't see much value in messing with them.

We could mention MFA at L3 for 7.5.1 and 7.5.2 but I don't know if it is really necessary. Feels a little too prescriptive.
In the context of a situation where an external Identity Provider is used, then there should be some TOTP in use, in my opinion.

> Why specifically in that case?

* Not user-friendly to ask for multi-step authentication, especially when this is something that the user needs to do repeatedly and/or frequently. Which makes it a bit unrealistic to ask.
* IdP is often also SSO - you can log in to the application without entering any credentials because you are using your SSO (e.g., gmail). How do you require MFA for approving certain actions in the application with that?
These sound like more reasons to avoid getting bogged down in this as I said here: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2883#issuecomment-2786325882
For each requirement, specify at least a single factor authentication. Think about wording.

Opened #2938.

I think changing authentication info should require full auth. The others I think a single factor is sufficient.
